macro.headline: Trend intact but VIX ticking up as oil-shock headlines hit the tape
macro.story:
The tape is holding its uptrend but showing tension under the surface. SPY sits at 754.95, up 1.4% on the week and 2.7% on the month, above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a neutral-to-firm RSI of 59.5 and a positive MACD. QQQ is also above both moving averages but its MACD has rolled negative, so leadership is narrowing. The VIX popped 9% in a single session to 16.4 and is up 5% on the week even as the VIX3M/VIX ratio remains in contango near 1.24 — a market that is nervous, not panicked. Meanwhile WTI oil jumped 3.8% today (+8% on the week), gold and silver are down 2–5%, DXY is grinding higher, and the 10-year yield sits at 4.57%. Under the hood, S&P 500 breadth is soft: only 26.5% of names bullish versus 38.4% bearish, and 7 of 11 GICS sectors are above their 50-day.

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation attributes the oil spike and VIX pop to fresh geopolitical stress — chart reads and posts flag a Strait of Hormuz closure narrative, US military headlines, and WTI breaking out of a 71–72 consolidation to 74+ on the day. Sentiment on the broad indices is genuinely split: one camp is bearish on QQQ, MU, and semi-cap equipment, arguing individual-stock volatility is running far hotter than the headline VIX suggests (a chart read cites an S&P 500 constituent-vol index near 49 versus headline VIX near 15 — a record gap). Another camp leans firmly bullish on AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, META, ARM and the AI-compute stack, pointing to a generational shift in hyperscaler and semi free-cash-flow. This is consistent with what the sector data shows — Financials, Healthcare, and the S&P index score highest while Materials weaken and Tech has slipped to NEUTRAL with a bearish MACD despite still holding above its 50-day. The sentiment narrative and the price data broadly agree: risk-on trend intact, but with visible cracks in tech leadership and a real geopolitical bid under oil.

Rotationally, the leadership is rotating toward Financials (score 9.2, RSI 65.8, hot), Healthcare (8.8, hot), and Utilities/Industrials as qualifying tailwinds — while Tech and Discretionary are neutral and Materials is outright weak. The Early-Runway rotation signal is confirmed in Diagnostics & Research, Health Information Services, Staffing & Employment, Credit Services, Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Internet Content, and Software-Application — a validated tailwind for names that sit in those industries with the continuation setup geometry in place. The DXY-strength / metals-weakness inverse relationship is playing out cleanly today (DXY up, gold/silver down), so precious-metals longs face a validated headwind.

Forward watch: (1) whether the VIX pop extends past 20 — that would cap macro confidence and demand tighter risk; (2) whether QQQ's negative MACD resolves down (leadership crack) or reverses; (3) whether the oil bid holds or fades as headlines evolve; (4) whether soft breadth (only 26.5% bullish) improves to confirm the index-level uptrend or diverges further.

**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength paired with a grinding rise in the belly and long end of the curve is the dominant force this week, and it's silently reshaping every risk trade underneath the surface. DXY sits at 100.96, above both its 21d and 50d SMAs with the DXY_METALS_TAG signal ACTIVE, while 10Y yields have pushed to 4.58% and 5Y to 4.32%, both with RSI north of 60 and vs50 posture positive. The tape looks calm — SPY +2.7% on 21d, VIX 16.48 in contango — but the composition of leadership (Financials, Insurance, credit-sensitive value) is telling you the bid is coming from a higher-for-longer rates regime, not a broad risk melt-up.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** Regime reads BULL with 8/10 confidence, VIX term structure in contango front-to-3M (16.48 → 18.57), and breadth at 63.6% above 50SMA — the macro scaffolding is intact. But the ACTIVE DXY signal is the load-bearing item: with dollar in a confirmed uptrend, Gold (-6.8% vs50, RSI 40), Silver (-16.3% vs50, RSI 37), and the entire precious complex are getting compressed exactly as the backtested inverse (corr -0.45, holds in 70% of 24-month windows) would predict. 10Y at 4.58% is trending higher, not ceilinged — the signal explicitly DOESN'T HOLD, so treat this as a directional yield tape, not a reversion setup. Same discipline on Oil at 74.10 (RSI 43, WTI mean-reversion has no edge) and TLT at 84.47 (RSI 40, mean-reversion DOESN'T HOLD) — both in trends, neither a fade.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** XLF (+6.6% 21d, +6.0% vs50) is the clean leader and it maps directly to the spine — steeper curve, higher belly yields, life and P&C insurers repricing book yields. XLV (+4.5%) is the co-leader with idiosyncratic drivers. Underneath, industry rotation is flowing INTO Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and one unmapped bucket — all ACCELERATING_BULLISH — while nothing has flipped out. Notably, the AI Infrastructure theme is in CHASING stage at day 42 with health 8.0, and both Precious Metals and Broad Commodity themes are officially FADING with multiple invalidators triggered — the data has shifted, no thesis-anchoring on commodities here.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The extended trades that have already run: Semiconductors (HOT 13 months, +258% — literally the max on record, CEILING flagged) and Internet Retail (+17.4% on 21d). These are manage-exits situations, not fresh-entry setups. The in-range, smart-money-flow names are where the asymmetry sits: **NTAP** (coil 98.9%, bullish flow) and **TWLO** (coil 95.9%, bullish flow) in early-innings Software Infrastructure (HOT only 1 month vs 7-month typical); **AAPL** (coil 99.3%, bullish flow) in Consumer Electronics riding the accelerating leg; **PINS** (coil 91.7%) in Internet Content & Information, also 1 month into a spell that typically runs 6. These four coilers are the cleanest expression of participating in the leadership without buying the ceiling.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY 101.80 resistance against SPY 758.45 resistance. If dollar breaks 101.80 while SPY stalls at 758, the spine tightens further — expect metals to break support (Gold 4031, Silver 57.03), Semis to finally give back, and the coiling software names to be the safest place to be long. If DXY rolls back under 100.56 support instead, the spine snaps and the Gold/Silver washouts become playable — but respect that 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so no all-clear on one green candle.
